Summary and stance: The Committee judged that the labor market continued to strengthen and overall activity expanded at a moderate pace. Inflation moved closer to the 2 percent symmetric objective, though core measures remained somewhat below 2 percent and market-based inflation compensation stayed low. With near-term risks roughly balanced, the FOMC raised the federal funds rate target range to 3/4 to 1 percent, maintained reinvestments, and signaled a gradual path of further increases with policy remaining accommodative for some time. Future moves will remain data-dependent across labor, inflation, and financial conditions.

FSR overlay: The Financial Stability Report points to generally resilient core financial institutions and contained near-term funding risks, but it also highlights elevated asset valuations, pockets of leverage in parts of the nonfinancial sector (including CRE and some nonbank activities), and occasional market liquidity vulnerabilities. These considerations temper the otherwise constructive macro backdrop, supporting the Committee’s gradualism and vigilance toward inflation and financial conditions.

Net read: Modestly positive growth and labor trends with cautious normalization, tempered by identified financial stability vulnerabilities.
